title: Bookkeeper
description:
Sophia at Avocet Legal Careers is pleased to be working with a well-established organisation seeking an experienced Bookkeeper to join its finance support team.

This is a part-time, home-based opportunity offering flexibility, autonomy and regular travel across Cornwall.

About the Client

Our client is a respected organisation with a widespread presence across Cornwall. They support a network of sites throughout the county and are committed to delivering a high standard of financial management and operational support. The organisation offers a welcoming culture, flexible working arrangements and the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution within a varied and people-focused role.

About the Role

Working from home for 28 hours per week, you will take responsibility for maintaining accurate financial records across a portfolio of locations. The position combines bookkeeping, reporting, stakeholder support and occasional compliance monitoring. Regular travel throughout Cornwall is required, with mileage paid from home at 55p per mile, paid travel time and a monthly car allowance of 80.

Bookkeeper Responsibilities
- Maintaining accurate bookkeeping records for multiple sites using cloud-based finance systems
- Processing income and expenditure transactions and reconciling bank accounts
- Monitoring financial records and following up on missing information where required
- Producing year-end financial information and supporting reporting processes
- Providing guidance and practical support to stakeholders responsible for local finances
- Delivering training and assistance on financial processes and record-keeping requirements
- Assisting with reviews, audits and compliance checks across various locations
- Responding to finance-related queries and building positive working relationships across the organisation

Bookkeeper Requirements
- AAT qualification, part-qualified status or equivalent bookkeeping experience
- Previous experience in a bookkeeping or finance support position
- Strong numerical accuracy and excellent attention to detail
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
- Confident communication skills with the ability to support a range of stakeholders
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities
- Comfortable working independently and managing your own workload
- Full driving licence and access to your own vehicle
- Willingness to travel regularly throughout Cornwall

Benefits
- Salary of 27,503.84 per annum
- Home-based working
- 28-hour working week
- 20 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays (pro rata)
- Additional time off during the Christmas period
- Company pension scheme
- Death in Service benefit
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Cashback and employee discount scheme

The Ideal Candidate

You will be an experienced and dependable bookkeeping professional who enjoys combining financial accuracy with stakeholder support. You'll be comfortable managing your own workload, travelling regularly across Cornwall and building trusted relationships with people at all levels.

For a confidential discussion about this opportunity, please contact Sophia at Avocet Legal Careers.

title: Administrator
description:
Plant & Parts Administrator

Location: Redruth
Salary: 25,000 - 28,000 per annum
Hours: Monday to Friday, 08:00 - 17:00

We are seeking an organised and proactive Plant & Parts Administrator to join our busy team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong administrative skills and an interest in stock control, plant, fleet, or stores management.

Working as part of the Plant Department, you will play a key role in ensuring parts, tools, and equipment are accurately managed and readily available to support operational requirements.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist with the day-to-day management and organisation of the plant and parts stores.
- Monitor, track, and record stock levels, including plant parts, tools, and fleet-related items.
- Maintain accurate inventory records and update internal databases and management systems.
- Support the implementation and continuous improvement of stock-control and parts-management systems.
- Assist with ordering, receiving, checking, and storing parts and equipment.
- Liaise with site teams to understand requirements and ensure parts and equipment are available when needed.
- Communicate with suppliers and colleagues to support the efficient movement and distribution of stock.
- Carry out regular stock checks and investigate discrepancies.
- Maintain an organised stores environment, ensuring all items are correctly labelled, recorded, and stored.
- Provide general administrative support to the Plant Department, including data entry, filing, and record management.
- Support the wider team with additional duties as required.

About You
- Previous experience in an administrative, stores, stock control, plant, fleet, or parts environment would be advantageous.
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Confident using Microsoft Office and internal computer systems.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritise workloads effectively.
- Good communication skills with the ability to build positive working relationships with colleagues and suppliers.
- Accurate data entry and record-keeping skills.
- A proactive and flexible approach to work.
- Ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary of 25,000 - 30,000, depending on experience.
- Full-time, permanent position.
- Monday to Friday working hours with no weekend work.
- Opportunity to join a supportive and growing team.
- Ongoing training and development opportunities.

If you are an organised administrator looking for a varied role where you can make a real impact within a busy Plant Department, we'd love to hear from you. For more information or to apply for this Plant & Parts Administrator position, please contact Louise Fletcher, Berry Recruitment, on (phone number removed).

We are committed to fair and inclusive recruitment. All applicants will be considered on the basis of their skills, experience, qualifications and ability to perform the role, and no applicant will be treated less favourably because of a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010.

title: Plant Administrator/Coordinator
description:
Plant Administrator/Coordinator

Location: Redruth Cornwall
Salary: Competitive, depending on experience
Job Type: Full-time Permanent
Sector: Plant / Construction / Logistics

Join the Team

We re looking for an organised and proactive Plant Parts & Stock Coordinator to join our growing Plant department.

This is a brand-new role and a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys logistics, organisation, stock management and working in a busy operational environment.

You ll play an important role in helping manage plant parts, tools and equipment across the business, supporting teams across multiple live sites throughout the South.

The Role

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing and maintaining Plant stores and stock.
- Monitoring stock levels and identifying when parts or equipment need to be ordered.
- Tracking and logging plant parts, tools and equipment.
- Liaising with teams across multiple live sites.
- Supporting the wider Plant team with administration.
- Keeping accurate records of equipment and stock movements.
- Helping coordinate the movement of parts, tools and equipment between sites.
- Supporting the introduction and management of new systems.
- Ensuring stock and equipment records are kept accurate and up to date.
- Helping improve organisation and efficiency across the Plant department.

About You

We re looking for someone who is:
- Highly organised with good attention to detail.
- Confident coordinating multiple tasks and priorities.
- Interested in logistics, stock control and equipment management.
- A good communicator who is comfortable liaising with different teams.
- Confident using computers and learning new systems.
- Proactive and able to work independently.
- Reliable, flexible and willing to get involved.
- Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.

Previous experience in plant, construction, logistics, stock control, stores or fleet would be advantageous, but transferable experience in organisation, coordination and administration will also be considered.

Why Join Us?
- Brand-new role with the opportunity to make it your own.
- Competitive starting package.
- Ongoing training and development.
- Opportunity to progress your career within a growing business.
- Varied role working across multiple sites and teams.
- Opportunity to help develop new systems and processes.

Apply Now

If you re organised, practical and enjoy logistics, stock management and coordinating people and equipment, we d love to hear from you.

Apply today to take the next step in your career with MJL.

title: Project Administrator
description:
We re looking for a proactive and organised Project Administrator to play a key role in supporting our Project Managers and Engineers, helping to deliver projects efficiently and successfully from start to finish.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with strong administrative and IT skills who thrives in a fast-paced environment. You'll enjoy coordinating multiple priorities, building strong relationships with colleagues, suppliers and customers, and making a genuine impact on the success of our projects.

Key Responsibilities
- Providing administrative support to project and operational teams
- Liaising with suppliers and assisting with procurement activities
- Raising requisitions and purchase orders through electronic procurement systems
- Checking goods received against orders and ensuring compliance with quality, environmental and safety standards
- Coordinating internal and external plant and equipment hires
- Assisting with project documentation, asset management records and project close-out information
- Supporting the production and distribution of Operation & Maintenance manuals, CDM compliance documentation and product manuals
- Managing project files, safety files and work packs
- Printing and controlling drawings, specifications and project documentation
- Supporting Project Managers and Engineers with ad-hoc project administration tasks

Skills and Experience
- Strong administration experience within a busy office environment
- Excellent IT skills, including Microsoft Office Suite
- Exceptional organisational and time management skills
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- Ability to prioritise workloads and meet deadlines
- Self-motivated with a proactive "right first time" approach
- Comfortable working both independently and within a multi-disciplinary team

What we
- Competitive salary and benefits package
- Career development and progression opportunities
- A growing business with long-term project opportunities
- A supportive and collaborative working environment
- A company that genuinely values the wellbeing of its people

About Us

We are MARCH . The leading provider of critical engineering services. Supporting the industries we all rely on to improve their infrastructure, process, and digital environments. We work together with our customers to maintain business continuity, optimise output, and drive new standards in productivity, reliability, and sustainability. We help deliver operational resilience, increased performance, and better environmental outcomes, across the board.

Why March?

Progress is People.

MARCH has ambitious plans and central to our future growth is attracting, developing and retaining the very best talent. Whether your role is onsite or office-based, engineering or support, we offer opportunities for all our people to develop their careers and maximise their potential. MARCH is committed to building teams that reflect a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. We believe diverse thinking strengthens engineering, and we welcome applications from all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process, just let the team know.

title: Team Administrator
description: You will be supporting the Risk and Safety Team and additional teams within the Integrated Governance directorate. This is a varied role, providing a comprehensive administrative service that will include the management of work programmes, diaries, meetings and Trust systems relating to staff and finance. The post holder will be required to manage and prioritise their day-to-day workload and use their initiative, without direct supervision, for routine tasks. This will require good organisational skills and the ability to work to tight deadlines and with frequent interruptions. Please note:If you are an internal candidate and wanting to apply for this position as a secondment opportunity. Before applying, please ensure you have discussed the post with your current line manager and obtained their agreement to support your release for the duration of the secondment. The post will act as a first point of contact for internal and external stakeholders The postholder will be required to work with a degree of flexibility to enable attendance at, and support to, committee meetings. This will include the administration and minute-taking of some directorate meetings. Theywill regularly update the Head of Risk and Safety about workload and workflow. The post holder will ensure prompt attention is given to enquiries from staff, patients, visitors and colleagues from partner agencies.
